control: TLS 1.3 mutual authentication and exact peer certificate pin; uint32 BE canonical JSON <=65536 bytes; nine methods (hello, register_ingress, admit, resolve_contributors, bind_context, open_relay, close_turn, release_session, evict_scope)

readiness.lifetime: private 0600 exclusive-create, fsync before serving, refuse existing record; endpoint launcher supplies this exact boot ID to its pinned consumer

admit.context_reuse_semantics: when an active completed bound context for (owner, proposed_context_id, key, scope_incarnation, context_epoch) exists on this host and optional prior_generation/context_generation (if supplied) matches that bound generation, admit reuses that generation ID for same-generation complete-contributor context reuse; if scope_incarnation or context_epoch rotated, or the prior turn did not complete, admit mints a fresh generation ID

resolve_contributors.semantics: resolves unseen prior-turn/history contributor delivery references on an admitted unbound capsule via NativeReader.Resolve with purpose='contributor' without inserting into seenDeliveries ingress replay tombstones, enabling complete-contributor bind_context while allowing those references to be resolved or admitted independently across turns

bind_context.core_hash: bytes/sha256 cover canonical JSON of exactly context_id, context_generation, originals; originals are complete native Headers, including the invoking original and all resolved contributor Headers
bind_context.chunk_semantics: each bind_context frame uses manifest containing the chunk descriptor; bytes/hash fixed on first chunk, offset exactly accepted length, standard base64 <=32768 decoded bytes recommended; no truncation/replacement/path/URL; canonical full core verified before binding
bind_context.contributor_resolution: if optional contributor_references/delivery_references are supplied on bind_context before final chunk assembly completes, the host resolves any not-yet-resolved contributor references on the capsule via purpose='contributor' before verifying ObservedHeader and Stage1 contributor intersection

tls_metadata.semantics: populated when include_tls_trust=true and host relay TLS trust material is configured; never disables TLS 1.3 verification

open_relay.http: production URL is HTTPS over PublicationTLSListener (TLS 1.3); handle is a 64-hex one-turn bearer; worker verifies private CA and/or leaf cert_sha256 with InsecureSkipVerify=false
open_relay.stdio: actual pinned CLI executes --turn-relay <handle>; handle is unpadded base64url of a closed JSON ticket <=512 characters containing endpoint, token, and optional ca_file, cert_sha256, server_name; ServeTurnRelay enforces TLS 1.3 with InsecureSkipVerify=false, custom RootCAs from ca_file/SSL_CERT_FILE, and VerifyConnection leaf cert_sha256 pinning
open_relay.relay_executable: private config may name the pinned CLI; empty selects this executable; absolute regular non-writable executable required
open_relay.bearer_domain: 64 lowercase hex characters; ordinary bf_/app_/uk_ credentials are rejected by the relay ticket parser

host_config_optional_relay_tls.defaults: ServePermissionHost defaults relay_ca to peer_ca and relay_cert_sha256 to the SHA-256 of the loaded server leaf certificate when not explicitly overridden

native_reader_bounds.saturation_behavior: fail closed with permission: bundle unavailable (PERMISSION_BUNDLE_UNAVAILABLE); never evicts read_id/read_nonce uniqueness fences or HeaderV1 immutability observations via TTL or sliding window

verification: exact pinned endpoint control sources (e4601041 and afb732b2) and v44 convergence harness exercised over mTLS 1.3, private-CA TLS 1.3 PublicationTLSListener relay, actual CLI --turn-relay process, and ServePermissionHost v2 package bootstrap with page-bounds-v2.json enforcement
rpc_identity: JSON-RPC IDs only correlate replies; equal parameters and reused IDs may be legitimate new logical calls. Each BeginCall mints a private call ID and each prepared physical attempt is one-use. Native delivery replay is separately fenced; no argument-based idempotency is invented.
